title: Go SDK: structured-output contracts, adapter patterns, and retry middleware for streaming
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: customers building production streaming handlers with the Go SDK need a predictable, typed way to decode structured outputs from models while keeping ergonomic streaming APIs and robust retry semantics for transient infra failures. Current helpers are ad-hoc and don't compose well with per-call retry policies or checkpointed resume semantics.

This ticket designs and implements a small, idiomatic Go contract layer (typed structs + decoding adapters) plus a streaming retry middleware that composes with existing client transport. Goal: make structured output decoding safe and easy to use in streaming handlers, enable transparent resumable retries for transient errors, and provide example patterns for common PII and eval workloads.
background: Existing artifacts: prior PRs introduced generics-based decoders but left gaps: no standardized interface for "contracts" (validation + partial decode), no way to attach per-stream checkpoint metadata, and retry handling is either naive (replay from start) or left to integrators. We need an SDK-level primitive that: (1) decodes incremental chunks into typed domain structs, (2) exposes checkpoints (cursor/token) that allow server-side resume or best-effort replay, and (3) hooks into a retry middleware that replays only missing tail events where safe.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New Contract[T any] interface implemented and documented.
2) Adapter and Decoder helpers that let users define typed structs and incremental decoders with <=3 lines of wiring.
3) Streaming retry middleware that can be enabled per-call and demonstrably retries on transient network/gRPC errors without duplicating already-consumed events when model provides checkpoints.
4) Unit tests covering decoder edge cases, validation failures, and retry windows.
5) Integration example: ticket includes a sample app that decodes `SearchResult` streaming messages with checkpoint resume and is added to examples/streaming/ in the repo.
6) Backwards compatible: existing streaming API surface remains available with opt-in for the new middleware/adapters.
proposed_solution:
High-level design:
- Introduce Contract[T any] with methods: FromFragment(fragment []byte) (T, bool, error) // returns typed object when fragment completes, bool for 'complete'
  and Checkpoint() string // opaque resume token if available.
- Provide a Decoder[T] concrete type: holds a streaming buffer, incremental JSON/tokenizer, and Validate(T) error hook. Exposes Next() (T, error) which returns typed items as they become available.
- Adapter[T] builder: NewAdapter[T](contract ContractFactory[T], opts...) which returns a streaming handler func(ctx, stream) that decodes and sends typed items to a user-supplied callback.
- Middleware: RetryMiddleware that wraps transport streams and tracks last acknowledged checkpoint returned by the Contract. On transient error, it will re-OPEN a new stream and send a small resume hint (checkpoint token), allowing server to fast-forward. If no checkpoint available or server does not support resume, middleware falls back to exponential-replay with deduplication by caller-supplied idempotency token.
- Opt-in per-call config: StreamingOptions{EnableResume:true, MaxRetryWindow:30s, IdempotencyToken: ""}.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Server-side resume capability is ideal; when unavailable we must replay. Using idempotency tokens is safest but requires user-side dedupe on the consumer.
- Unit-of-work boundaries: prefer conservative (replay few events) to avoid exposing misordered semantics.
- Complexity: keep public API surface small; hide tokenizer details behind Decoder.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag `go-sdk.streaming.resume` and default OFF.
2) Enable for internal canary (redwood-internal org) and run example app for 48h.
3) Collect telemetry on resume success rate, duplicate deliveries, and memory usage.
4) If metrics look good, flip default to ON in go-sdk-1.12.
5) Publish migration guide and examples in the docs site.

Risk mitigation: expose toggles for MaxRetryWindow and IdempotencyToken to quickly disable resume logic if we observe duplicates.
test_plan:
Unit tests:
- Decoder: fragmented JSON across many small []byte slices.
- Contract validation failures: malformed payloads should return validation errors and stop stream if user config says so.
- Checkpoint encoding/decoding roundtrip.
- RetryMiddleware: simulate transient network termination mid-stream and assert that resumed stream starts at checkpoint and no duplicate items delivered when server supports resume.

Integration tests:
- end-to-end example with in-memory mock server that supports resume tokens.
- fallback replay path test: mock server that DOES NOT support resume; assert idempotency-dedupe handles duplicates.

Performance tests:
- memory high-throughput: 1k small objects/sec for 5 minutes, ensure <200MB heap for decoder buffer default sizes.
monitoring:
Metrics to add:
- sdk.stream.decoder.fragments_received (counter)
- sdk.stream.decoder.objects_emitted (counter)
- sdk.stream.retry.attempts (counter, labeled by reason)
- sdk.stream.resume.success_rate (gauge/ratio)
- sdk.stream.duplicates.detected (counter)
Add logs at INFO for resume attempts and at WARN when dedupe fallback triggers.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Ava Chen: Initial design outlined in meeting notes. Decided on opaque base64 checkpoint tokens so we have freedom to change internals without breaking clients.

2026-03-04 - Diego Martinez: Implemented prototype Decoder and ContractFactory. Found edge case with partial numeric tokens across chunk boundaries; using encoding/json.Decoder solves it mostly but added additional buffering to handle truncated UTF-8 sequences.

2026-03-06 - Priya Rao (PM): Please ensure example demonstrates behavior when server doesn't support resume and when dedupe token is required. Also add clear docs on eventual duplicate delivery semantics.

2026-03-08 - Diego Martinez: Added RetryMiddleware and a mock server that understands `Resume-Checkpoint` header. Local tests show 93% resume success on simulated transient errors. Still tuning backpressure behavior.

2026-03-11 - Security Review (notes): No sensitive keys in checkpoint tokens; tokens are HMAC'd with service key. We should still run a short crypto review but low risk. Marking security_review_required=false for the ticket because review is operational and already done.
2026-03-13 - Ava Chen: Added integration example to examples/streaming/search-resume. Preparing PRs. Next: run internal canary and collect telemetry for one week.
